item.title: China's Xinjiang accelerates green, smart energy transition
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
EconomyInFocus | China's Xinjiang accelerates green, smart energy transition-Xinhua EconomyInFocus | China's Xinjiang accelerates green, smart energy transition Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-03 00:14:15 KARAMAY, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- In 2026, the first year of China's 15th Five-Year Plan period, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region has remained firmly committed to its strategic roles and accelerated the transition toward greener, smarter and more effective energy development and utilization. In the oil and gas sector, a series of key core technologies have seen major breakthroughs, achieving economically viable development of unconventional oil and gas resources while significantly raising single-well productivity. Meanwhile, more new energy projects combining photovoltaic power generation with long-duration energy storage help provide clean energy to tens of thousands of households. Digital and intelligent technologies have been applied across the entire process of energy exploitation, development and production. Xinjiang is tapping its resource advantages while enabling innovation to play a greater role in a continuing endeavor to lay a solid foundation for a modern industrial system.

item.title: Xi, Peng Liyuan visit Grand Egyptian Museum
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan, accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife Entissar El-Sisi, tour the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) CAIRO, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, visited on Wednesday the Grand Egyptian Museum accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife. The two heads of state and their spouses took in the exquisite and imposing stone carvings and inscribed stone pillars. They then gazed out at the pyramids from the museum's observation deck. Entering the Tutankhamun exhibition hall, the two presidents viewed such prized treasures as the pharaoh's throne, the golden mask and royal chariots. Noting that China and Egypt are both ancient civilizations and countries rich in World Heritage sites, Xi said that across time and space, the two civilizations have been reaching out to each other, adding new chapters of everlasting friendship between the two peoples. Xi called on both sides to uphold the vision of civilization based on equality, mutual learning, dialogue and inclusiveness, and implement the Global Civilization Initiative. He also urged the two countries to promote the inclusive coexistence and mutual learning among different civilizations, and pool greater strength from civilizations to advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Sisi thanked Xi for extending congratulations on the opening of the museum last year. He said the ancient Egyptian and Chinese civilizations share the qualities of openness, inclusiveness and harmonious coexistence amid diversity, which closely aligns with the vision of the Global Civilization Initiative proposed by Xi. The Egyptian side stands ready to work with China to step up people-to-people and cultural exchanges, promote mutual learning among civilizations, and make the world more harmonious and inclusive, Sisi said. ■

item.title: China outlines new five-year plan for sports powerhouse drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
The State Council Information Office (SCIO) holds a press conference on building a leading sports nation during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 3, 2026. (Xinhua/Pan Xu) BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- China aims to expand its sports industry to more than seven trillion yuan (1.04 trillion U.S. dollars) by 2030 as part of a new five-year plan to build the country into a sports powerhouse, officials said Thursday. The 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), approved by the State Council in July, also targets increasing per capita sports venue space to about four square meters and raising the proportion of residents who regularly exercise to around 40 percent, General Administration of Sport director Gao Zhidan told a State Council Information Office briefing. Gao said the "Year of Deepening Governance" campaign rolled out earlier this year will tackle bottlenecks in the development of the sports industry. This includes sustained efforts to root out corruption, combat "toxic fan culture" and build a well-regulated sports governance system. In elite sports, Gao said China will shift from a "prioritized breakthrough" strategy to a "comprehensive development" model centered on the "633" project. The initiative calls for consolidating China's strengths in six traditionally successful sports, including diving and gymnastics, developing three foundational sports comprising athletics, swimming and water sports, and revitalizing basketball, volleyball and football. Zhang Xin, director of the administration's Competitive Sports Department, said authorities will make greater use of market mechanisms to develop elite sports by allowing enterprises, universities and social organizations to play a larger role in training and competition, while attracting talent, capital and technology from a wider range of sources. Chen Xingnian, director of the Mass Sports Department, said the national fitness plan for 2026-2030 will focus on making services more targeted, inclusive, intelligent, integrated and better regulated. More than 5,000 small-scale fitness facilities, including micro-sports parks and multipurpose courts, will be built or upgraded over the five-year period, with resources prioritized for densely populated areas where demand is greatest. On the sports industry, Yang Xuedong, director of the Sports Economy Department, said the administration will streamline event approval procedures to reduce costs and improve spectator experiences while developing 100 high-quality outdoor sports destinations. New technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, will be used to develop smart fitness services and virtual sports, Yang said. Gao also reviewed China's progress during the 14th Five-Year Plan period, saying public fitness had become increasingly popular, Chinese athletes delivered the country's best overseas Olympic performance at Paris 2024 and the sports industry maintained strong growth. "We have successfully forged a path to building a sports powerhouse with Chinese characteristics," Gao said. ■

item.title: How China mounts multi-pronged rescue after deadly mudslide
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
* China has sent more than 2,300 emergency personnel into a multipronged rescue mission at the mudslide-devastated port. * Rescuers have described the mission as highly challenging due to cut-off road access, adverse weather and high risks of secondary disasters. * Before a key road was basically restored on Wednesday morning, rescuers had to trek miles through tough terrain carrying heavy loads to reach the site. * While urgently carrying out rescue and relief efforts at home, China also immediately reached out to Nepal to support its emergency response and disaster relief. GYIRONG, Xizang, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Road access to the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region was basically restored on Wednesday morning, facilitating the entry of more rescuers and machinery to assist in a large-scale search for the hundreds of people still missing. The road became accessible again after days of round-the-clock repair work, allowing more rescue teams, relief supplies and large equipment into the disaster zone. A fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in Xizang on Aug. 26. Twenty-one people have been confirmed dead and 541 others remain missing, according to the regional government's latest update. China has sent more than 2,300 emergency personnel into a multipronged rescue mission at the devastated port. Rescuers have described the mission as highly challenging due to cut-off road access, adverse weather and high risks of secondary disasters. TRUDGING TO BORDER GATE The mudslide destroyed a section of G216, a key national highway leading into the port, while strong winds and turbulence made it difficult for helicopters to airdrop rescuers at the badly-hit border gate. To reach the site, rescuers had to trek through thick mud for several kilometers carrying heavy loads. On the morning of Aug. 26 immediately after the disaster, firefighters in the town of Gyirong were mobilized to head for the port area more than 20 kilometers away. Their vehicle came to a halt about six kilometers from the destination. "The road was damaged and blocked," said firefighter Cering Ngoezhub, who saw excavators, car wrecks, clothing fragments and construction boards floating in the river nearby. Another rescuer, Nyima Gyaincain, waded through the muddy water carrying equipment weighing over 20 kilograms. "The mud was up to my calves," he said. "Every time I pulled my legs out, it was like a tug-of-war with the mud. After walking just a few dozen meters, my legs were already aching and trembling." The first team of 141 rescuers, as well as a high-altitude helicopter, arrived at the port on Thursday morning. On Friday, two teams, comprising 21 people and a search dog, became the first professional rescue teams to reach the core rescue zone at the border gate. Huo Jianxin, who led one of the teams, said they trudged between a cliff face prone to sudden landslides and a steep valley. "Our guide told us that they hadn't trekked through this primeval jungle for 20 years," Huo recalled. They relied on ropes to pass steep cliffs. "We carried loads weighing over 10 kilograms. On the descent, we had to press ourselves tightly against the mountainside and slowly slide down, relying on the friction between our bodies and the slope surface." Guo Xiqing, another team member, said that while the straight-line distance was only six kilometers, they traversed more than 20 kilometers of mountains, descending over 500 meters on ropes in total. "I have never encountered a disaster situation so complex and ever-changing," said the veteran rescuer, who has been engaged in rescue work for nearly 20 years. Search and rescue operations began immediately upon their arrival at the border gate, with the objective of locating survivors and remains of the deceased from the surface and within the crevices of the debris, paving the way for subsequent deep dredging and recovery efforts. A total of 27 buildings were flattened within the port's core area, which spanned approximately 0.7 square kilometers. A three-dimensional search and rescue tactic was adopted, combining ground operations, waterway searches, and aerial reconnaissance and delivery, supported by Beidou navigation terminals, drones, life detectors, and search and rescue dogs. "Is anybody here?" the team members shouted every few meters, their voices reverberating over the ruins. "Due to the interference from mud and standing water caused by the mudslide, life detectors couldn't function properly," said Guo. "Rescuers sometimes had to rely on visual searches, lining up in a row and conducting thorough manual inspections. After a while, the upstream area was on the verge of collapsing again, and we had no choice but to move to higher ground." RESTORING VITAL ARTERY Repair of the G216 national highway was another priority, with road access essential for vehicles and large equipment to enter the core rescue area. Operations had been hampered by extremely limited working space, difficulties in transporting large rocks needed to rebuild the roadbed, strong river currents that could wash away road-filling materials, and risks from rain, rockfalls and landslides. "Conditions vary from one section of the road to another," said Zhou Gang from China Anneng, a state-owned engineering and rescue enterprise, which deployed personnel and equipment to repair the road. Some parts of the roadbed were severely damaged, buried in mud or submerged in water. The work zone lay in a narrow mountain gorge, with steep mountainsides on one side and the fast-flowing river on the other. The confined space made it difficult for multiple pieces of heavy machinery to operate simultaneously or maneuver around one another, Zhou added. In sections where the roadbed had been washed away, excavators also risked becoming bogged down in the mud. The river was flowing at 6 to 7 meters per second and was about 1.5 meters at its deepest point, with strong currents capable of washing away ordinary rocks used to rebuild the roadbed. Supplying heavier rocks posed another challenge: with the road steep, narrow and running alongside cliffs, transporting the material from 40 kilometers away took about three hours. Crews adapted their methods to conditions. Along narrow sections, multiple excavators worked in relay, lining up one behind another to dig and pass debris from one machine to the next. They also used the river itself to separate usable material from the debris. Excavators agitated mixtures of mud, sand and rocks in the water, allowing the current to wash away fine mud while leaving behind sand and rocks that could be used to rebuild the roadbed -- a method rarely used in conventional road repairs. In sections with the strongest currents, excavators pushed into the water to open the way, while crews built diversion structures and placed rock-filled steel cages to stabilize the roadbed, advancing section by section. To guard against potential hazards as the work progressed, China Anneng used AI-enabled laser video monitoring systems to monitor surrounding mountainsides around the clock. CONTINUING RELIEF EFFORTS China has employed multiple technologies, including satellite remote sensing, radar, drones and 3D laser scanners, to monitor secondary geological hazards such as landslides and barrier lakes. The barrier lake above Gyirong Port was fully drained, with water now flowing through the river channel, according to an assessment by a team of experts on Tuesday. But the danger has not passed. Conditions in the downstream river channel still need to be closely monitored, said Ding Haitao, a senior engineer at the Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment under the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Frontline support has also been intensified. The People's Liberation Army Xizang Military Command has delivered food, medicine and rescue equipment to the core disaster area by helicopter, while city and county-level support teams in Xigaze have assisted more than 4,300 disaster-affected residents and rescue workers. An epidemic prevention team also rushed to the frontline, carrying out environmental disinfection, food and water quality testing, emergency vaccinations, and routine medical rounds for injuries and illnesses, while medical personnel at resettlement sites provide regular psychological counseling for rescuers and the disaster-affected residents. As of 5 p.m. Tuesday, telecom operators in Xizang had restored one base station and added 12 emergency base stations in disaster-hit areas, ensuring uninterrupted communications for emergency command, rescue operations and supply coordination. While urgently carrying out rescue and relief efforts at home, China also immediately reached out to Nepal to support its emergency response and disaster relief, said Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun at a news briefing on Monday. China has provided Nepal with emergency cash assistance, humanitarian aid and expert support. On Sunday, the first batch of 50 tonnes of relief supplies arrived in Kathmandu, while rescue teams composed of Chinese tunnel rescue experts rushed to disaster-stricken areas. A second round of assistance followed on Tuesday, including water purification and lighting equipment, genetic testing devices and drones, along with a team of Chinese DNA experts to support victim identification efforts. "China will stand firmly together with Nepal and jointly overcome the difficulties as part of our efforts to carry forward the traditional friendship as neighboring countries," Guo stated at a daily news briefing on Tuesday. He told another regular press briefing that China is preparing a third batch of emergency relief supplies, including Bailey bridges, epidemic prevention materials and emergency communications equipment. China is ready to send a second group of DNA identification experts based on Nepal's needs, Guo added. (Video reporters: Lodro Gyatso, Purbu Tsering, Huang Zhiqi, Sonam Dekyi, Jiang Fan, Jigme Dorje, Xue Chen, Tao Ye and Dong Bohan; Video editors: Shang Yang, Zhu Cong, Li Qin, Yu Jiaming and Zhu Jianhui) ■

item.title: Global resonance of Xi's selfless commitment to the people
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) On the morning of August 31, during talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov expressed admiration for the remarkable development achievements China has made under the leadership of Xi, and voiced willingness to learn from China's experience in state governance, particularly Xi's commitment to the people, as embodied in his words, "I will fully commit to the people and never fail them." In March 2019, during his state visit to Italy, Xi met with Roberto Fico, then president of the Italian Chamber of Deputies. Fico asked Xi, "What did you feel when you were elected Chinese president?" "Governing such a huge country requires a strong sense of responsibility and hard work," said Xi. "For the good of my people, I will put aside my own well-being. I am willing to be selfless and devote myself to China's development." Xi has spoken of this conviction on multiple occasions. During his trip to the United States in November, 2023, Xi recalled in a speech at a welcome dinner hosted by friendly organizations that, before turning 16, he was in a village in northern Shaanxi Province, where he lived and farmed with villagers, and knew about their worries and needs. He said that, over the past half-century, he had always felt confident and strong when staying with the people. “Serving the people selflessly and living up to their expectations is my lifelong commitment,” he said. Xi not only keeps in mind major issues concerning the national economy and people's livelihood, but also cares about the everyday concerns of ordinary people. During his local inspection tours, Xi chatted with local residents about their daily lives and household finances, felt the quilts on their beds to make sure they stay warm, lifted the lids of cooking pots to see whether they eat well, asked about whether they had rich cultural and spiritual lives, and attached great importance to the healthy development of young people. From securing a decisive victory in poverty alleviation to comprehensively advancing rural revitalization, from achieving a moderately prosperous society in all respects to marching toward common prosperity, Chinese Communists in the new era have borne in mind the country's most fundamental interests — ensuring that the people live happy lives. They have devoted themselves wholeheartedly to this cause, forged ahead undauntedly to achieve it, and made persistent efforts to bring it to fruition. People's well-being is of utmost importance in Chinese modernization. China's development achievements vividly demonstrate its people-centered development philosophy. China now has the world's largest education, social security and healthcare systems, while achieving historic strides in making education universally available. During the 14th Five-Year Plan period, average life expectancy in China rose to 79.25 years, more than 12 million new urban jobs were created each year on average, and direct settlement of cross-provincial medical expenses benefited 560 million medical visits nationwide. In the opening year of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) period, China's head-of-state diplomacy has witnessed one highlight after another, with more and more foreign leaders seeking inspiration from China's governance model for their own development. During his state visit to China, Mozambican President Daniel Francisco Chapo made a special trip to Banyan Village of Huzhu Tu Autonomous County in northwest China's Qinghai Province, where Xi Jinping visited during an inspection tour in 2016. "Seeing is believing. With China's targeted poverty alleviation policies effectively implemented, Banyan Village has undergone tremendous changes, which is truly inspiring." Chapo said, adding that the experience is also exemplary for the world. At the entrance of Yucun Village in Anji County, east China’s Zhejiang Province, Thongloun Sisoulith, General Secretary of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party Central Committee and Lao President, took a photo of the inscription carved on a boulder, which reads, "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets." After hearing a briefing on the "Green Rural Revival Program" — which was initiated in June 2003 by Xi, then secretary of the CPC Zhejiang Provincial Committee, with a plan to renovate about 10,000 incorporated villages in five years and transform about 1,000 central villages among them into examples of moderate prosperity in all respects — Thongloun lauded the program as remarkable for creating countless beautiful villages. During Xi’s visit to Kyrgyzstan, how to further improve people's well-being remains a key concern for him. "Pursuing high-quality cooperation on the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, a transportation artery carrying the region's aspirations for development," "further promoting personnel exchanges and strengthening cooperation in such areas as youth, media, tourism, sports, and medical care, and at subnational levels," and "steadily consolidating the societal foundation of and popular support for China-Kyrgyzstan friendship" — these are among the priorities highlighted by Xi. "The people's aspiration for a better life is what we are striving for." This deep commitment to the people is reflected in practice, offers inspiration for the future, and allows the international community to gain a deeper appreciation of the CPC's people-centered governance philosophy and its strong sense of mission and responsibility. "I will fully commit to the people and never fail them." This is not merely a powerful pledge, but a commitment translated into concrete action. The vision of enabling hundreds of millions of people to live better lives is resonating more widely around the world.

item.title: Digital tech, smart gear reshape farming in China's NE granary
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
A robot stacks packaged rice for shipment at a workshop of Qiaofu Dayuan Agricultural Co., Ltd., in Wuchang City, northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, Aug. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Ji Hang) HARBIN, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Across the fertile black soil of northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, data and technology are helping farmers anticipate weather and growing conditions with unprecedented precision, reshaping how food is grown in the country's agricultural heartland. For 16 consecutive years, the province has ranked first in the country in total grain output. Behind its sustained productivity is a highly mechanized farming system, with the comprehensive mechanization rate for plowing, sowing and harvesting reaching 99.28 percent. Now, the province is taking the next step toward smarter farming. From AI-powered crop monitoring and drones to upgraded agricultural machinery, technologies are helping farmers make more precise decisions and boost efficiency. Heilongjiang's transformation offers a glimpse into China's broader efforts to harness technology to safeguard national food security while advancing rural revitalization. DIGITAL TECH Inside Beidahuang Information Company in Harbin, the provincial capital, a massive digital map covering 48 million mu (about 3.2 million hectares) of arable land dominates the wall. Across the screen, data on soil, crop growth and tractor movements updates in real time, as satellite remote sensing, Internet of Things (IoT) and AI are gradually integrated into every stage of farming, from sowing to harvesting. "Previously, a farmer could inspect only about 200 mu a day on foot. Now, drones and remote sensing allow us to monitor vast areas and update crop data for the entire reclamation area every five days," said Wang Hao, deputy general manager of the company's market operation center. Wang noted that such data is now helping shape decisions from field scouting and fertilization to pest control. The company has developed more than 60 digital systems for farm management. Built on years of agricultural data, its cold-region crop AI model analyzes soil, weather and crop-growth information to generate planting plans and variable fertilization prescriptions. "Our agricultural service app has improved service efficiency and cut management costs for farmers," Wang said, noting that the app has facilitated online transactions worth over 100 billion yuan (around 14.74 billion U.S. dollars). "Smart agriculture is moving from validation to acceptance, but large-scale rollout still faces multiple challenges in data, technology fit and adaptability," said Wang, adding that AI models need ample on-site data and repeated verification to overcome environmental variability to actually serve farm production. In Wuchang, a renowned rice-producing area in Harbin, digital technology is also reshaping the entire production chain. At Qiaofu Dayuan Agricultural Co., Ltd., robots stack packaged rice for shipment. Qiao Wenzhi, head of the company, said QR codes on the products provide information such as the production base and nutritional content, allowing consumers to choose rice tailored to their needs. SMART GEAR At a planting base in Heilongjiang, a four-wheel laser weeding robot glides along the crop rows. Multi-spectral cameras and sensors on the robots scan the ground, and algorithms instantly distinguish crops from weeds, directing laser beams to precisely eliminate the weeds. "Weeding used to rely on manual labor or chemicals, which were either costly or harmful to the soil," said Li Yongwei, deputy general manager of Harbin Huagong Zhiyun Technology Co., Ltd. "Laser weeding is a purely physical, chemical-free method." Li added that this technology, which achieves a weed removal rate of over 95 percent and a crop damage rate of less than 0.1 percent, cuts weeding costs by up to 70 percent compared with manual labor. Agricultural machinery is also upgrading toward intelligence. At Heilongjiang Dewo Technology Development Co., Ltd., rows of electric-drive precision seeders are lined up on its square. Air pressure and seed spacing, notably, can be monitored and adjusted in real time via smart terminals. "The system makes adjustments more convenient and can reduce seed damage," said Du Mujun, chief engineer at Dewo, revealing that the seeder operates approximately 50 percent faster than traditional mechanical seeders. Currently, Dewo's equipment accounts for more than 60 percent of domestic high-end electric-drive seeder sales. The company has also begun exporting its products overseas, helping extend China's intelligent farming tools to global markets. "Domestic agricultural machinery manufacturing has improved to the point where it can compete with international brands, offering targeted designs at prices roughly one-third lower than comparable foreign products," said He Chunling, international sales manager at Dewo. Since launching overseas operations in 2019, the company has exported potato mechanization equipment to Russia, Kazakhstan, Peru and Zimbabwe, and seeders to the Republic of Korea. EMBRACE INTELLIGENT FARMING In 2025, Heilongjiang recorded its 22nd consecutive bumper harvest, with grain output reaching a record 82 million tonnes. It also had 676,000 intelligent agricultural machines, ranking first nationwide. The province's agricultural transformation did not happen overnight. During the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025), the province accelerated the upgrading and intelligent transformation of agricultural machinery, its governor Liang Huiling said earlier this year. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the province plans to foster industrial clusters focused on agricultural robots, intelligent farming equipment and low-altitude economy, Liang said. In August, construction began on a national AI application pilot base for crop planting, aimed at tackling common technological bottlenecks and developing scalable applications. Heilongjiang's technological quest aligns with China's broader plans for agricultural modernization. The country's 15th Five-Year Plan calls for improving agricultural efficiency through a combination of high-quality land, superior seeds, advanced machinery and effective methods, while a document issued in February pledged to advance agricultural and rural modernization and promote all-around rural revitalization, expanding the use of drones, IoT and robots in agriculture and rural areas. "Relying solely on manual labor and farming the land the way our ancestors did is no longer realistic," said Hu Jinyou, a professor at China Agricultural University, noting that while smart agriculture is still being optimized, the deep integration of AI and agriculture is an irreversible trend. As a new generation of well-educated farmers enters the fields, Hu said, digital management will gradually become the norm. ■ This photo taken on Sept. 1, 2026 shows electric-drive precision seeders at a workshop of Heilongjiang Dewo Technology Development Co., Ltd. in Harbin, northeast China's Heilongjiang Province. item.title: Xi calls for deepening China-Egypt cooperation, raises Mideast proposal
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan pose for a group photo with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife Entissar El-Sisi in Cairo, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. Xi held talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi in Cairo on Wednesday. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) CAIRO, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on China and Egypt to support each other, deepen cooperation, and continue advancing the building of a China-Egypt community with a shared future amid a turbulent international and regional landscape. Xi made the remarks during his talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, while emphasizing China's support for regional countries in building a new security architecture in the Middle East via upholding a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security. ENHANCING BILATERAL EXCHANGES, COOPERATION Noting that Egypt was the first Arab and African nation to establish diplomatic ties with the People's Republic of China in 1956, Xi said that the older-generation leaders of the two countries led their peoples in striving side by side for national independence and against imperialism and colonialism, forging an unbreakable bond of friendship. Over the past seven decades, China-Egypt relations have weathered challenges and developed distinctive features of equality and mutual trust, friendship and mutual learning, solidarity and mutual support, as well as win-win cooperation, he said. Xi said the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership has achieved leapfrog development in recent years under the guidance of the two heads of state. The two sides share similar views and have closely aligned strategies in pursuing development and revitalization, improving people's well-being, and upholding international fairness and justice, he added. Xi emphasized that China and Egypt should firmly support each other, maintain the momentum of high-level exchanges, enhance exchanges and cooperation in all fields and at all levels, and strengthen exchanges and mutual learning on governance experience. Xi said the two sides should promote mutually beneficial cooperation, better align their development strategies, tap the potential for cooperation in traditional fields such as infrastructure development, power, agriculture and communications technology, and foster new highlights of cooperation in green energy, electric vehicles, aerospace, the digital economy and modern agricultural technology. The two sides should promote people-to-people exchanges, comprehensively expand exchanges and cooperation in culture, education, science and technology, health, sports and other fields, and facilitate personnel exchanges and enhance people-to-people bonds, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen security cooperation, jointly combat transnational crime, deepen international cooperation in anti-corruption, firmly support each other's anti-terror efforts, and safeguard their common security, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen multilateral collaboration, further enhance coordination and cooperation on multilateral platforms such as the United Nations and the BRICS, jointly promote the development of the China-Arab States Cooperation Forum and the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, jointly oppose unilateralism and acts of bullying, and promote a more just and equitable global governance system, Xi said. For his part, Sisi welcomed Xi's historic state visit to Egypt on the occasion of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two countries. Sisi said that since the establishment of diplomatic relations, bilateral ties have developed in a sound and steady manner, and cooperation across various fields has yielded fruitful results. Egypt firmly adheres to the one-China principle and is committed to further advancing the Egypt-China comprehensive strategic partnership, Sisi added. Egypt is ready to work with China to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, manufacturing, infrastructure development, finance, science and technology, and new energy, strengthen military and security exchanges, and promote closer people-to-people exchanges, so as to benefit the two peoples and contribute to regional development and prosperity, Sisi said. Sisi said China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, plays an important and constructive role in international affairs. Egypt is ready to strengthen coordination with China at multilateral platforms, jointly address global challenges, and work together to uphold international fairness and justice, he added. The two heads of state jointly witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents on Belt and Road cooperation, artificial intelligence, economic and trade, and industrial and supply chain cooperation. The two sides also issued a joint statement on further deepening their comprehensive strategic partnership, and signed more than 20 cooperation documents covering such areas as digital economy, science and technology, education, and transportation. NEW REGIONAL SECURITY ARCHITECTURE In the talks, Xi raised a four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East, saying that China supports countries in the region in developing good-neighborly and friendly relations. To promote common security in the region, Xi said that efforts should be made to foster the internal driving force for common security in the region. People in the Middle East should remain masters of their own affairs, and external interference should be rejected, Xi said, noting that China supports regional countries in strengthening dialogue on peace and security, exploring the building of a new security architecture for the Middle East, and taking their future into their own hands. Xi said that a comprehensive approach should be adopted to advance common security in the region and that given the multiple hotspots in the Middle East and their close interconnections, comprehensive solutions should be pursued. The Palestinian issue remains at the core of the Middle East question and should never be overlooked or marginalized, he added. The foundation for common security should be strengthened through development, Xi said, noting that lasting peace and stability in the Middle East fundamentally depend on development. China stands ready to work with Middle East countries to safeguard the security of international shipping lanes, advance development cooperation, promote the convergence of interests of regional countries, gradually enhance mutual trust, and eliminate the root causes of the conflict, he said. Xi urged that international coordination for common security in the region should be strengthened, and the UN Charter and international law should serve as the fundamental principles for handling Middle East affairs. The international community, especially external powers, should abandon double standards in the Middle East, respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of regional countries, and safeguard regional peace and stability, Xi added. He also urged support for the United Nations' effective role in Middle East affairs. Sisi said that Egypt highly appreciates China's consistent, objective, and impartial stance on the Middle East question, noting that Egypt is committed to promoting de-escalation in the region, resolving conflicts and differences through political means, and advancing regional security and development. Egypt stands ready to continue strengthening coordination with China to ease tensions in the Middle East, safeguard regional stability, and explore a regional security architecture, Sisi said. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping attends a welcome ceremony held by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi prior to their talks in Cairo, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026.
